title: Mangle Names
statement: Implement `solve(class_name, attr)`. If `attr` starts with `__` and does not end with `__`, return the mangled name `_{class}__rest` where class is `class_name` with leading underscores removed. Otherwise return `attr` unchanged. `__init__` is not mangled. `__balance` on `Account` becomes `_Account__balance`.
constraints: Leading underscores on the class name are stripped
hints: The mangled form applies only when the name starts with two underscores and does not end with two.
Strip leading underscores from the class name.
Prefix one underscore, the class, then the original attribute including its underscores.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Name mangling is a textual transform the compiler applies to identifiers in the class body.

editorial: Name mangling is a textual transform the compiler applies to identifiers in the class body. It is not a security boundary. __balance becomes _Account__balance so a subclass does not overwrite it by accident. __init__ ends with double underscores and is left alone.
